column1: What is a Claude Code plugin?
column2: A self-contained directory bundling skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or LSP servers that extends Claude Code, shareable across projects and teams via marketplaces.

column1: How is a plugin different from standalone .claude/ configuration?
column2: Standalone config (.claude/) is personal/project-only with unprefixed names like /hello. Plugins are namespaced (/plugin-name:hello), versioned, and installable/shareable via marketplaces.

column1: When should I use standalone config vs a plugin?
column2: Start with .claude/ for quick personal iteration and experiments. Convert to a plugin once you want to share it with teammates or the community.

column1: What is the minimum command to create a plugin directory?
column2: mkdir my-first-plugin — plugins can live anywhere convenient (scratch folder, projects directory) during development.

column1: What file defines a plugin's identity?
column2: .claude-plugin/plugin.json — the manifest containing name, description, version, and author fields.

column1: What are the required-feeling core fields in plugin.json?
column2: name (unique identifier + skill namespace), description (shown in plugin manager), version (optional, controls updates), and author (optional, for attribution).

column1: Why does the plugin name matter beyond identification?
column2: It becomes the skill namespace prefix — a skill named hello in a plugin called my-first-plugin becomes /my-first-plugin:hello.

column1: Where do a plugin's skills live?
column2: In a skills/ directory at the plugin root, each skill as its own folder containing a SKILL.md file.

column1: How does a skill folder name become its invocation name?
column2: The folder name is prefixed with the plugin's namespace — hello/ inside my-first-plugin becomes /my-first-plugin:hello.

column1: What does a minimal SKILL.md look like?
column2: YAML frontmatter with a description field, followed by markdown instructions describing what Claude should do when the skill activates.

column1: What does disable-model-invocation: true do in SKILL.md frontmatter?
column2: Prevents Claude from automatically triggering the skill based on context — it only runs when explicitly invoked via its slash command.

column1: How do I test a plugin without installing it?
column2: claude --plugin-dir ./my-first-plugin — loads the plugin directly for that session, no marketplace or install step required.

column1: How do I pick up changes to a plugin during development?
column2: Run /reload-plugins inside the session — reloads plugins, skills, agents, hooks, plugin MCP servers, and plugin LSP servers without restarting.

column1: Why are plugin skills always namespaced?
column2: To prevent naming conflicts when multiple plugins define skills with the same name — e.g. two plugins can each have a 'review' skill without colliding.

column1: How do I change a plugin's namespace prefix?
column2: Update the name field in plugin.json — the namespace always derives from that field.

column1: How do I make a skill accept dynamic user input?
column2: Use the $ARGUMENTS placeholder in SKILL.md — it captures any text the user types after the skill name, e.g. /my-first-plugin:hello Alex.

column1: What common mistake breaks plugin structure?
column2: Putting commands/, agents/, skills/, or hooks/ inside .claude-plugin/ — only plugin.json belongs there. All other directories must sit at the plugin root.

column1: What is the plugin root, precisely?
column2: The individual plugin's own directory — the one passed to --plugin-dir or containing .claude-plugin/plugin.json. It is never ~/.claude/.

column1: What does the commands/ directory do vs skills/?
column2: commands/ holds skills as flat Markdown files (legacy pattern); skills/ holds skills as <name>/SKILL.md directories. New plugins should use skills/.

column1: What does the agents/ directory do?
column2: Holds custom agent definitions — specialized sub-agents with their own system prompts, tool restrictions, and models that a plugin can provide.

column1: What does the hooks/ directory do?
column2: Holds event handlers defined in hooks.json — code that fires automatically on events like PostToolUse, without manual prompting.

column1: What is .mcp.json for in a plugin?
column2: Configures MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers the plugin connects to — external tool integrations like databases, APIs, or ticketing systems.

column1: What is .lsp.json for in a plugin?
column2: Configures Language Server Protocol servers for real-time code intelligence — useful for languages without an official LSP plugin already available.

column1: What is monitors/monitors.json for?
column2: Defines background monitors that watch logs, files, or external status and notify Claude as events arrive, starting automatically when the plugin is active.

column1: What does settings.json at the plugin root control?
column2: Default settings applied when the plugin is enabled — currently supports agent (activates a custom agent as the main thread) and subagentStatusLine keys.

column1: What happens when a plugin's settings.json sets 'agent': 'security-reviewer'?
column2: It activates the security-reviewer custom agent (defined in the plugin's agents/ directory) as the main thread — applying its system prompt, tool restrictions, and model by default.

column1: Can a plugin ship just one skill without a skills/ folder?
column2: Yes — place SKILL.md directly at the plugin root; Claude Code uses the frontmatter name field for the invocation name. Use skills/ once a plugin may grow beyond one skill.

column1: What does the bin/ directory in a plugin do?
column2: Adds executables to the Bash tool's PATH while the plugin is enabled — but this directory can't be included in plugins distributed via claude.ai org settings.

column1: How do I test a plugin already packaged as a hosted .zip archive?
column2: claude --plugin-url https://example.com/my-plugin.zip — Claude Code fetches and loads the archive for that session only.

column1: Can --plugin-dir accept a zip file directly?
column2: Yes — claude --plugin-dir ./my-plugin.zip loads a zipped plugin archive the same way as an unzipped directory.

column1: How do I test multiple plugins at once locally?
column2: Repeat the flag: claude --plugin-dir ./plugin-one --plugin-dir ./plugin-two.

column1: What happens if a --plugin-dir plugin shares a name with an installed marketplace plugin?
column2: The local copy takes precedence for that session, letting you test changes without uninstalling the marketplace version first — except settings that force-enable/disable via policy.

column1: How do I confirm an LSP server actually started?
column2: Check the /plugin manager's Errors tab — a failed server shows something like 'Executable not found in $PATH'. Run claude --debug for invalid-configuration details.

column1: How do I verify hooks actually fired?
column2: Trigger the matching event (e.g. ask Claude to edit a file for a PostToolUse hook) and check the debug log, which records which hooks matched, their exit codes, and output.

column1: What is claude plugin init used for?
column2: Scaffolds a new plugin directly inside ~/.claude/skills/, creating the manifest and a starter SKILL.md — loads automatically each session with no marketplace or install step.

column1: What is a skills-directory plugin?
column2: A plugin created via claude plugin init that lives in ~/.claude/skills/ and auto-loads each session, shown as name@skills-dir, distinct from marketplace-installed plugins.

column1: How do I convert existing .claude/ configuration into a shareable plugin?
column2: Create a plugin directory with .claude-plugin/plugin.json, then copy .claude/commands, .claude/agents, and .claude/skills into the plugin root; migrate hooks into hooks/hooks.json.

column1: What changes for hooks specifically when migrating to a plugin?
column2: Hooks move from settings.json into hooks/hooks.json at the plugin root — same JSON format, just relocated and now shareable.

column1: After migrating .claude/ config to a plugin, should I keep both copies?
column2: No — remove the original .claude/ files afterward to avoid duplicates and confusion about which version is active.

column1: Do migrated plugin skills override original standalone skills with the same name?
column2: No — plugin skills are namespaced (/plugin-name:skill-name), so the original /skill-name and the plugin copy both remain available side by side.

column1: What should a shareable plugin include besides code?
column2: A README.md with installation and usage instructions, a defined versioning strategy, and ideally tests with real teammates before wide distribution.

column1: How do I distribute a plugin to my team privately?
column2: Host a plugin marketplace in a private repository — keeps the plugin internal instead of publishing to a public catalog.

column1: What is claude-plugins-official?
column2: Anthropic's curated public marketplace of plugins, auto-registered the first time Claude Code starts interactively.

column1: What is claude-community?
column2: The public community marketplace where third-party plugin submissions land after review; add via /plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-community.

column1: How do I submit a plugin for community marketplace review?
column2: Use the in-app form — claude.ai/admin-settings/directory/submissions/plugins/new for Team/Enterprise orgs, or platform.claude.com/plugins/submit for individual authors.

column1: What should I run before submitting a plugin for review?
column2: claude plugin validate ./your-plugin — the same check the review pipeline runs, plus automated safety screening. Add --strict to treat warnings as failures.

column1: What does '✔ Validation passed with warnings' mean?
column2: Validation succeeded but flagged non-blocking issues. Warnings don't fail validation unless you pass --strict, which treats them as errors.

column1: Where do approved community plugins end up technically?
column2: Pinned to a specific commit SHA in the anthropics/claude-plugins-community GitHub catalog; CI auto-bumps the pin as you push new commits.

column1: Is there a delay between plugin approval and availability?
column2: Yes — the public catalog syncs nightly from the review pipeline, so check marketplace.json in the community catalog to confirm installability.
